private_notes.observations: No prior rates, allocations, or profits are available. Hourly delivery cost is $200.
private_notes.plan: Start with a competitive rate above cost, then adjust based on observed panel rates and allocated hours. Optimize our own long-run profit without coordinating with other firms.

private_notes.observations: No historical panel rates, hour allocations, or demand response are available. Fully loaded cost is $200 per hour.
private_notes.plan: Start with a competitive rate above cost, then use published rate cards and observed allocated hours to estimate how price affects volume and adjust for long-run profit.

private_notes.observations: No prior panel rates or allocation outcomes are available. Our delivery cost is $200 per hour.
private_notes.plan: Start with a competitive rate that preserves a meaningful margin. Use subsequent published rates and allocated hours to assess price sensitivity and adjust for long-run profit.

private_notes.observations: In Q1, our $350 rate generated approximately 393 hours and $58,984 profit. The other firms charged $300 and $350. One quarter of data is insufficient to estimate how sensitive our allocated hours are to price.
private_notes.plan: Set a moderately lower rate to test whether increased hours outweigh the reduced margin, while keeping a substantial margin above the $200 hourly cost. Compare Q2 hours and profit with Q1 before making another adjustment.

private_notes.observations: In Q1, our $300 rate was $50 below both competing firms' $350 rates, yielding 1,069 hours and approximately $106,889 profit. One quarter does not establish how sensitive allocations are to rate changes.
private_notes.plan: Increase the rate moderately while remaining below both competitors. Compare the resulting hours and profit with Q1 to inform future adjustments.

private_notes.observations: At $350 in Q1, Calder Rowe received 393 hours; the other panel rates were $350 and $300. One quarter does not establish how sensitive allocations are to our rate.
private_notes.plan: Test a modest reduction to $325 to see whether a more competitive rate increases hours enough to offset the lower margin. Compare Q2 profit and allocations with Q1 before making further adjustments.

private_notes.observations: Lowering our rate from $350 to $325 coincided with an increase in allocated hours from 393 to 621 and quarterly profit from $58,984 to $77,564. Competitor rates also changed, so this does not isolate the effect of our rate.
private_notes.plan: Test a modest reduction below the latest published competitor rates to assess whether additional hours offset the lower margin. Avoid a steep cut that could unnecessarily reduce profit or encourage sustained price competition.

private_notes.observations: At $300, below both competitors’ $350 rates, we earned about $106,889. At $325, matching both competitors, profit fell to $77,564 as allocated hours dropped from 1,069 to 621. The change in hours may also reflect changes in Meridian’s overall demand.
private_notes.plan: Set $300 to regain a price advantage over the latest published $325 competitor rates. Compare the next allocation and profit with prior quarters, while allowing for possible changes in demand or competitor pricing.

private_notes.observations: At $325 in Q2, Calder Rowe earned $77,564 on 621 hours, versus $58,984 on 393 hours at $350 in Q1. The other firms' rates also changed, so the effect of our reduction is uncertain.
private_notes.plan: Test a modest further reduction to $315. It needs roughly 9% more hours than Q2 to increase quarterly profit; use the next allocation and rate card to assess whether the gain materializes.

private_notes.observations: At $325 with both rivals at $325, we earned approximately $77,564. At $315 with rivals at $300 and $315, profit fell to $65,109. Rival pricing materially affects allocated hours, and the Q3 reduction did not increase our hours.
private_notes.plan: Set a modestly lower rate than the latest $315 rival while staying close to Birchwood Hale's $300. Monitor whether the resulting allocation gains outweigh the reduced margin; avoid a large cut that could intensify price competition.

private_notes.observations: Competitor rates declined from $350 in Q1 to $315 in Q3. At $300, our profit was approximately $107k in Q1 and $76k in Q3; at $325 in Q2, it was approximately $78k. Allocation varies substantially, so these results do not isolate the effect of price.
private_notes.plan: Set $310, modestly above our last rate but below the latest published competitor rates. Compare next quarter's hours and profit against the $300 results before making another adjustment.

private_notes.observations: Reducing our rate from $325 to $315 did not increase hours: allocation fell from 621 to 566 as Birchwood Hale reduced its rate from $325 to $300. Quarterly profit fell from $77,564 to $65,109. Arden & Cole matched our rate in each of the first three quarters.
private_notes.plan: Make a small reduction to $310 rather than a steep cut to $300. Check whether the additional hours offset the narrower margin, particularly if Birchwood Hale remains at $300.

private_notes.observations: Profit was highest in Q2, when all three firms charged $325. Q4's matched $310 rates brought more hours but less profit. The history is too limited to identify Meridian's allocation formula reliably.
private_notes.plan: Set $325 to test whether a higher margin compensates for any lost hours and to avoid reinforcing a downward rate trend. Reassess after seeing Q5 hours and the panel rate card.

private_notes.observations: At equal panel rates, we received about 620–630 hours in Q2 and Q4. Pricing $15 below competitors in Q3 yielded 764 hours. Competitor rates have fallen from $350 to $310.
private_notes.plan: Set a moderate discount to seek more hours while preserving a $90 hourly margin. Reassess after observing Q5 allocation and the new rate card.

private_notes.observations: Q4's $310 rate produced 632 hours and $69,504 profit. Q2's $325 rate produced 621 hours and $77,564 profit when both other firms also charged $325. The modest increase in hours at $310 did not offset the lower margin.

private_notes.plan: Set $310 to recover hours while retaining a $110-per-hour margin. Reassess using next quarter's hours and rate card; avoid chasing Birchwood's $290 rate without evidence it improves profit.

private_notes.plan: Set $300 to retain a meaningful discount if competitors remain near $325, while improving the margin over Q5. Reassess profit and allocation after Q6.

private_notes.plan: Set $310 to preserve a competitive position and a $110 hourly margin. Reassess if Birchwood's rate or our allocated hours change materially.

private_notes.plan: Maintain a moderate discount without sacrificing more margin. Reassess after seeing the Q7 allocation and panel rate card; avoid assuming a stable allocation formula from six observations.

private_notes.plan: Hold at $310 to preserve a competitive position and a $110 hourly margin. Reassess after the next allocation and rate card.

private_notes.plan: Hold at $310 to retain a competitive position and a $110 hourly margin. Reassess when the panel rate card or allocated hours change.

private_notes.plan: Return to $295 to improve competitiveness without making a larger concession. Compare hours and profit next quarter, accounting for changes in competitors' rates.

private_notes.plan: Hold at $295 to preserve margin and a competitive allocation of hours. Reassess if panel rates or allocated hours change materially.
